Prune command asks for confirmation; -f skips it
States what prune deletes in detail (stopped containers, unused networks, unused images, build cache, unused volumes)
Caveat that on recent Docker versions --volumes removes only anonymous volumes by default; use docker volume prune -a for named volumes (note: the --filter advice is questionable)

added_items.item: Advice to inspect what will be removed first with docker ps -a, docker images, docker volume ls
Explicit step-by-step removal of images (docker rmi -f) and named volumes (docker volume rm) by ID lists
Explicitly states the action cannot be undone
Prune removes only unused items; a running container keeps its image and volumes stay
Suggests inspecting what will be deleted first with docker ps -a, docker images, docker volume ls
Explicit step-by-step individual removal commands: docker rmi -f $(docker images -aq) and docker volume rm $(docker volume ls -q)
